title: NHIS Health Inequality Trends
summary: Harmonized decades of NHIS survey data for a health-inequality trends study, with reproducible pipelines and automated checks that catch data failures before analysis.
overview: A long-running health-inequality trends study needs data that means the same thing across decades of survey redesigns. I built the harmonization and analysis infrastructure for it: cross-year variable mappings, reproducible pipelines and automated quality checks. The work supports a manuscript in preparation.
myRole: I led the harmonization and analytic workflow in coordination with the faculty investigator, from codebook design to pipeline automation and quality assurance.

sections.title: Data Harmonization & Reproducibility
content: Harmonized variables across decades of NHIS survey data, documenting every cross-year mapping in a codebook.
Built reproducible SAS, R and SQL pipelines across NHIS and NHANES survey waves, shortening the manual analysis cycle.

Built automated drift, cross-tabulation and missing-data checks into the pipeline, which caught documented failures, including cross-version inconsistencies and drift from the NHIS survey redesign, before analysis.

outcomes: Harmonized decades of NHIS survey data into an analysis-ready, documented resource.
Shortened the manual analysis cycle with reproducible pipelines.
Caught documented data failures before they reached analysis.
